subject.title: feat(plugins): support per-agent plugin installation with --agent flag

question: Should OpenClaw expose a public per-agent plugin install flag before runtime discovery and uninstall/update behavior are fully scoped by agent?
rationale: This is not just a storage change: the flag changes user expectations around plugin code execution, install identity, and agent isolation, and the linked canonical issue is already marked for maintainer product/security review.

options.title: Require the full scoped contract first
options.body: Block this PR until install, uninstall, update, discovery/activation, docs, and security proof all agree on the agent scope.

options.title: Narrow to hidden groundwork
options.body: Remove the public CLI flag and keep only maintainer-approved internal helpers/tests if staged storage work is still useful.

options.title: Defer to the canonical issue
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue design in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/97749.

recommendation.title: Require the full scoped contract first
recommendation.body: Block this PR until install, uninstall, update, discovery/activation, docs, and security proof all agree on the agent scope.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent substantial work on the same plugin install command and persistence surfaces makes this the strongest available routing signal.
